title: Photo-mediated performance change of a 1,8-dihydroxyanthraquinone-based Dy6 single molecule magnet

synthesis.procedure: A methanol solution (7.5 mL) of Dy(OAc)3·5H2O (0.05 mmol, 0.0167 g) was mixed with a DMSO solution (2.5 mL) of 1,8-dihydroxyanthraquinone (H2L1, 0.05 mmol, 0.0121 g) in an 18 cm Pyrex tube sealed at one end, and trimethylamine (35 μL) was added. The tube was sealed under vacuum, heated in an oven at 90 °C for three days, and slowly cooled to ambient temperature to give golden yellow crystals.
synthesis.temperature: 90 °C, then slow cooling to ambient temperature
synthesis.vessel_or_method: 18 cm Pyrex tube sealed under vacuum and heated in an oven (solvothermal)
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Slow cooling to ambient temperature afforded golden yellow crystals.

properties.summary: Discrete Dy6 cluster is a zero-field SMM. Solid-state emission is at 688 nm upon 630 nm excitation. Light irradiation (630 nm, 1 h for in situ magnetism) shortens the relaxation time and lowers Ueff/kB from 95(6) K to 83(3) K, attributed to partial substitution of terminal MeOH by DMSO. No hysteresis loop was observed.

material_class.structural_family: bicapped tetrahedral Dy6 after partial terminal MeOH/DMSO substitution

synthesis.procedure: Single crystals of 1 sealed in a capillary with a tiny amount of mother reaction solution or polybutene oil were irradiated for 30 min with a CEL-PF300-T8 xenon lamp (300 W). The structure of the resulting crystals is 1a, in which terminal CH3OH is partly replaced by lattice DMSO. No stoichiometric amounts are given for this transformation.

reagents.name: mother reaction solution or polybutene oil

synthesis.vessel_or_method: capillary tube; CEL-PF300-T8 xenon lamp, 300 W
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Irradiated single crystals of 1 were used directly for the structure of 1a.

properties.summary: The authors assign the light-tuned zero-field SMM response of irradiated 1 to this partially substituted structure. After irradiation, χmT is 78.17 cm3 K mol−1 at 300 K and 20.19 cm3 K mol−1 at 2 K, and Ueff/kB falls to 83(3) K with faster relaxation (τ 1.75×10−4 to 1.22×10−2 s). No separate luminescence data are reported for 1a.
